subject: sociology
topicName: The Role of the Family in Society

questions.question: Compare Functionalist and Marxist views of the role of the family.

points.text: Functionalism: the family benefits society (socialisation, emotional support). Marxism: the family benefits capitalism (producing workers, consuming products, ideological control). Key difference: Functionalism sees the family as serving everyone; Marxism sees it as serving the ruling class. Functionalism ignores exploitation; Marxism ignores the positive emotional aspects of family life.

questions.question: Evaluate the Feminist view that the family oppresses women.

points.text: Feminist evidence: women do most housework (dual burden); domestic violence affects 1 in 4 women; the family normalises women's economic dependence; the divorce rate shows women want to escape oppressive marriages. Counter-arguments: many women choose family life; family structures are becoming more equal (symmetrical family); men also experience domestic violence; not all families are patriarchal

questions.question: Assess which perspective provides the most useful understanding of the family in modern society.

points.text: Functionalism: explains social order but ignores conflict and exploitation. Marxism: explains exploitation but ignores the emotional value of family. Feminism: explains gender inequality but may neglect other inequalities and positive family experiences. Personal Life perspective: values lived experience but lacks critical analysis.
